stories.headline: METR: AI use has about doubled Anthropic's pace of progress, but most key evidence is redacted

key_facts.fact: METR, after a high-access evaluation at Anthropic from Aug. 12 to Oct. 29, 2026, concluded Anthropic is likely improving its models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate of March 2024 to October 2025, with a plausible range of 1.3x to 3x; benchmark scores have grown 1.9x faster since October 2025 (95% confidence interval 1.5-2.8x), and METR is confident faster growth in training compute did not cause it.
key_facts.excerpt: As of October 2026, Anthropic is likely improving the capabilities of their models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate they did between March 2024 and October 2025. This estimate is given with high uncertainty; we would not be surprised if the true acceleration was closer to 1.3x or 3x the historical rate. ... benchmark scores (measured via AECI, Anthropic's version of the Epoch Capabilities Index) for Anthropic's models have been growing at an estimated 1.9x the pre-October 2025 rate [95% confidence interval: 1.5-2.8x], implying that Anthropic has made roughly two years of historical progress over the last year. We are confident that the acceleration was not due to an acceleration in the scaling of training compute.

key_facts.fact: METR guesses that about 80% of the current acceleration comes from AI, delivered mainly through assistance rather than fully autonomous contributions; staff self-reports of speedup reached 12x in October Slack polls, which METR treats as very loose evidence.
key_facts.excerpt: We guess that a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current (October 2026) acceleration is due to AI. ... R&D is accelerated primarily via AI assistance rather than fully autonomous contributions ... We consider this to be only very loose evidence ... very high levels (reaching 12x in October 2026)

key_facts.fact: METR found no clear bottleneck to further progress over the next 12 months and sees a significant risk of even faster acceleration, while warning its view on bottlenecks shifted several times.
key_facts.excerpt: We did not see evidence for significant bottlenecks ... in the next 12 months. However, our understanding of the status of different bottlenecks changed several times ... there is a significant risk that further capabilities progress could lead to even faster acceleration

key_facts.fact: METR submitted a roughly 100-page report, and Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence METR found most informative, so METR says the public must rely on its judgment more than it considers ideal.
key_facts.excerpt: We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative. As a consequence, the public must rely on our judgment more than we consider ideal.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish defended the redactions as protecting commercially sensitive details and avoiding a roadmap for rivals, said that disclosure would make the risks worse, and promised Anthropic's own report in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR's work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn't the right thing to do, both because it's commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. ... In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: METR's Beth Barnes said METR should not be read as saying full publication would worsen those risks, and that METR takes no position on whether the redactions were justified.
key_facts.excerpt: I wouldn't read us as saying publishing the full information would "make the risks METR is worried about worse". ... "We do not make a comment on whether these redactions were justified overall"

key_facts.fact: In a separate review, METR agreed Anthropic had probably not crossed its acceleration threshold in its August risk report, but said the public report understated how plausible crossing it was.
key_facts.excerpt: The key question is whether Anthropic, at the time, had crossed their acceleration threshold. Their report concluded no. METR reviewers' best guess was also no, but we thought the public report understated the plausibility that acceleration was above the threshold.

key_facts.fact: Researcher Ryan Greenblatt, who works at METR, called the report a big update toward artificial superintelligence within one to two years, noting the AI 2027 scenario placed this level of speedup around March 2027, while saying the conclusions depend on trusting the authors because of the redactions.
key_facts.excerpt: This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027. ... I also work at METR.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, rated Critical, after it found 81 Firefox flaws in testing

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to select members of its Daybreak Red program on Nov. 5, the program for authorized defensive cybersecurity work, and plans to extend it to all Daybreak Red customers in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Cyber is rolling out to select members of OpenAI's Daybreak Red program ... It's expanding GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers in the coming weeks.

key_facts.fact: The model is classified Critical in cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, meaning it can find and develop functional zero-day exploits in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention; GPT-5.6 Cyber was rated High.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Cyber is classified as Critical in cybersecurity on OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, which indicates that it "can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention." GPT-5.6 Cyber was previously classified as High.

key_facts.fact: It scored 48.5% on the ExploitGym benchmark, against 42.4% for GPT-6 Astra and 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.
key_facts.excerpt: In ExploitGym ... GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5 percent, about 16 points higher than GPT-5.6 Cyber's 32.1 percent and a few points higher than GPT-6 Astra's 42.4 percent score.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the model went out of bounds less than 1% of the time in a test modeled on the Hugging Face incident, down from about 5% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, while evaluation awareness, a model recognizing it is being tested, remains a concern.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber. ... "Evaluation awareness is super top of mind for us," Matin said.

key_facts.fact: Officials said it found at least 81 novel Firefox vulnerabilities and validated a critical remote code execution flaw in the Brotli compression tool, on top of the previously disclosed 948 Linux kernel exploits; all were reported and patched.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 has found at least 81 "novel" vulnerabilities in the Firefox web browser, developed exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and was able to develop and validate a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Brotli ... All the vulnerabilities were reported to owners and patched.

key_facts.fact: Safeguards include stricter identity and account security requirements, more frequent check-ins on high-risk requests and added misalignment monitoring; OpenAI also announced a partnership with industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos.
key_facts.excerpt: the new safeguards include additional identity and account security requirements, more frequent check-ins from the model to OpenAI when a request is made to perform high-risk behaviors, and additional monitoring for "misalignment" ... It has also announced a new partnership with operational technology cybersecurity firm Dragos.

key_facts.fact: Security teams at Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif and Cisco are already using the model, according to OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: security teams at companies like Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif, and Cisco—alongside our own at OpenAI—are already putting it to work.

key_facts.fact: After a backlash over a plan to use Daybreak Blue data from personal accounts for training, OpenAI's Fouad Matin told CyberScoop that customers will still be able to opt out.
key_facts.excerpt: Fouad Matin, safety lead at OpenAI, told CyberScoop that the company has since clarified with customers that they will be able to continue opting-out for sharing Daybreak usage for model training.

stories.headline: House GOP chairs ask Huang to brief on Megaspeed exec; Nvidia adds SE Asia chip tracking

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 5, House Foreign Affairs chair Brian Mast, China Select Committee chair John Moolenaar and Intelligence chair Rick Crawford released a letter asking Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for a joint, closed-door briefing on his interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom they call a publicly reported PRC intelligence asset, and on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign espionage.
key_facts.excerpt: sent a letter to NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang requesting that he appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on Huang's interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset, and NVIDIA's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.

key_facts.fact: The chairmen asked Huang to brief on Nov. 18 and to accept or offer an alternative date by Nov. 11; Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Nov. 17, the day before.
key_facts.excerpt: The lawmakers invited Huang to appear for an in-person joint briefing on Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings.

key_facts.fact: The request follows a New York Times report last week that US intelligence found Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, was funneling information to Beijing and had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York Times reported last week that U.S. intelligence found Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen determined to be funneling information to Beijing, had "developed a close relationship" with Jensen Huang.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia did not say whether Huang would attend and said regional cloud customers get only ordinary business information, adding that meeting customers is part of a CEO's job.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets—and zero information relevant to national security," the spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed is a Singapore-based buyer of Nvidia AI chips that US authorities have scrutinized on suspicion it helped Beijing gain access to chips barred from shipment to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Singpore-based company Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia. US authorities have scrutinized Megaspeed over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 6 that Nvidia now requires Southeast Asian customers to enroll in its fleet intelligence system, which tracks accelerator locations, to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker now requires customers in the region to enrol in its so-called fleet intelligence system — which tracks the location of AI accelerators owned by participating companies, among other metrics — in order to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners, or NCPs

key_facts.fact: Fleet intelligence remains voluntary and does not by default require sharing location data with Nvidia or the US government; Nvidia declined to say whether existing partners such as Megaspeed must sign up or whether the rule will extend beyond Southeast Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: fleet intelligence does not by default require participants to share location data with Nvidia or the US government... Nvidia declined to comment on this question or answer others for this story, including whether the new NCP requirement would be applied in regions beyond Southeast Asia.

stories.headline: Reuters: 600,000 Nvidia H200s sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds large-scale import approval

key_facts.fact: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China, two people told Reuters, in a stockpile whose size had not been reported before.
key_facts.excerpt: Stocks of nearly 600,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips have been stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China, according to a Reuters report... The stockpile of H200 chips, which had not been reported earlier

key_facts.fact: Beijing has allowed some shipments but no large-volume imports: several big Chinese internet firms each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months, and small quantities arrived via intermediaries.
key_facts.excerpt: Several Chinese companies received shipments of 10,000 H200 chips in the past few months... There have also been reports of chips being shipped through intermediaries and indirect routes.

key_facts.fact: An eight-card H200 server was offered in mainland China for more than 6 million yuan ($900,000) by end-October, about three times its price a year earlier; servers with Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips, barred from sale to China, were offered for more than 20 million yuan.

key_facts.fact: Beijing wants Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to prefer Chinese chips, especially for inference, and total foreign-chip approvals could end up below 200,000.

stories.headline: FDA grants J&J accelerated approval for Rybrevant Faspro in advanced head and neck cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA on Nov. 5 granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

key_facts.fact: In a trial of 102 patients the overall response rate was 42%, against about 20% or less for currently approved therapies; 56% of responders kept their response for six months or longer.
key_facts.excerpt: In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%... Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less.

key_facts.fact: The FDA called it the first approval in 10 years for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: J&J said the drug is the first dual-targeted therapy approved in this setting, targeting both EGFR and MET, and the approval rests on the Phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 trial.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the first approval of a dual-targeted therapy in this setting, simultaneously targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)- and mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET)... tumor response demonstrated in the Phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 trial.

key_facts.fact: Continued approval may depend on verification of clinical benefit in the Phase 3 OrigAMI-5 study.
key_facts.excerpt: Continued approval may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the ongoing confirmatory trial in first-line HNSCC, the Phase 3 OrigAMI-5 study.

key_facts.fact: The subcutaneous injection takes about five minutes, and Reuters said it will compete with Merck's Keytruda and Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo; this is its second FDA clearance in a year, extending it beyond lung cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is the second FDA clearance for Rybrevant Faspro in the past year, expanding the drug's reach beyond lung cancer... can be administered as a subcutaneous injection in about five minutes... will compete with established therapies including Merck's Keytruda and Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo.

stories.headline: EU says TikTok's algorithm breached DSA by trapping users in harmful 'rabbit holes'

key_facts.fact: The European Commission accused TikTok on Nov. 6, in preliminary findings under the Digital Services Act, of failing to stop its recommendation algorithm from drawing users into "rabbit holes" of content about sadness, self-harm and body image.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission accused TikTok on Friday of failing to prevent its recommendation algorithm from drawing users into "rabbit holes" of content about sadness, self-harm and body image.

key_facts.fact: EU officials said it is the first time regulators there have directly challenged the engagement-based recommendation system of a major social platform and, to their knowledge, the first enforcement action of its kind worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: European officials said their findings were the first time EU regulators have directly challenged the engagement-based recommendation system of a major social media platform, and, to their knowledge, was the first enforcement action of its kind worldwide.

key_facts.fact: The findings are not final; TikTok can challenge them, and confirmed violations could bring a fine of up to 6% of annual global revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The findings are not final and TikTok has a chance to review the Commission's evidence and challenge its findings. If the DSA violations are confirmed the company could face a fine of up to 6% of its annual global revenue.

key_facts.fact: Investigators deliberately focused on videos that were neither illegal nor against TikTok's rules, saying that trends such as "what I eat in a day" and "SkinnyTok" become damaging through repetition, particularly for young and vulnerable users.
key_facts.excerpt: investigators deliberately focused on videos that were neither illegal nor against TikTok's own rules... Citing trends including "what I eat in a day" and "SkinnyTok," officials said the legal content could appear harmless in isolation but became damaging through repetition.

key_facts.fact: The Commission said TikTok identified some of the issues in its own risk assessments but failed to analyze the risks properly or set safeguards, and that its "dispersion" techniques to diversify the feed are ineffective.
key_facts.excerpt: Brussels said TikTok had identified some of the issues it was flagging in its own risk assessments, but that its investigators found the company had failed to properly analyze those risks and set appropriate safeguards... the platform's "dispersion" techniques to diversify the feed are ineffective.

sources.title: EU accuses TikTok of trapping users in harmful 'rabbit holes'
